tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS Verification Policy

TLS certificate verification is enabled in all builds of this project, including development builds, and it is not to be disabled for any build type. This sits alongside the project's standing rule that HTTPS is used everywhere, with no exceptions.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md
tool_input.description: Create the TLS verification policy doc

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md`. It says TLS certificate verification is enabled in all builds, development builds included, and must not be disabled for any build type. It adds that this goes with the standing rule of HTTPS everywhere, with no exceptions.

Both statements come from the project's current recorded decisions: "verification on all builds" and "https everywhere, no exceptions". The file doesn't mention the retired alternatives, which were disabling verification in dev builds and plain HTTP for internal hosts.

My first attempt to write the file through the shell failed with a parser error. I wrote it with the file-write tool instead, and it went through.

Muninn's heartbeat also reported 20 hook runs that started and never finished, which suggests a hook is exceeding its timeout. I didn't investigate; the details are in `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl`.
